title: GitHub estate audit and custom-code replacement
claim_boundary: Source-verified implementation only; higher evidence levels require the named open gates. Path presence is not behavioural proof; assertion-level traceability governs implementation claims.

assertions.statement: Run code/repository search for providers, PubMed, PRISMA, dedup and screening
open_gates: Run the scanner against current clones of every in-scope repository.
assertions.permitted_claim: Search-code patterns and a self-test exist; the whole estate was not rescanned locally.

assertions.statement: Populate migration manifest with exact files/owners/status
open_gates: Refresh exact revisions and owners before each migration.
assertions.permitted_claim: A source-verified migration inventory exists for observed repositories.

assertions.statement: Prioritise active research repos and shared skill repos
open_gates: Confirm priority with active project owners and current repository state.
assertions.permitted_claim: Priority and portfolio projections are prepared, not remotely applied.

assertions.statement: Create thin adapters or issues per repository
open_gates: Implement approved changes in each companion repository and run its native tests.
assertions.permitted_claim: Change packets and integration passports are prepared; companion repositories were not modified.

assertions.statement: Verify behavior before deletion and preserve provenance
open_gates: Dual-run old and new paths before deleting any custom code.
assertions.permitted_claim: No external custom code has been deleted.

assertions.statement: Re-run estate conformance and close superseded tracks
open_gates: Run estate conformance against current remotes and close only evidence-proven migrations.
